_doc: What the WEB PLATFORM is, as data: element capabilities, the ARIA state vocabulary, and the mapping from a contract's words to the platform's. Extracted verbatim from packages/react/src/emit/emit.mjs. This file is a TRANSCRIPTION, not a correction — where a list is incomplete against the W3C specification it is incomplete here too, and the `_note` says so. Completing one is a separate change with its own diff.
_boundary: Nothing framework-shaped may enter. `tabIndex`, `readOnly`, `className` and `htmlFor` are REACT's spellings of DOM names and belong in packages/react. The test is the mirror of @ds/contracts': if it would still be true in a Vue, Svelte or Lit backend rendering the same DOM, it belongs here.

defaults._doc: The element a backend reaches for when the contract names none. `activatable` is what a part declaring `activates` becomes; `container` is everything else.

div._note: The neutral container. Deliberately featureless: bears no role, is not focusable, takes no native state attribute. Listed rather than omitted so its emptiness is a statement rather than an oversight.

input._note: `implicitRole` is `textbox` only for a type-less or text input. This profile has no `type` axis, matching the emitter it was extracted from.

textarea._note: INCONSISTENT ON PURPOSE, preserved from the emitter. `implicitRole` says this element already announces as a textbox; `bearsRole` says an ARIA state attribute may not attach to it. Those cannot both be right. The emitter's role-bearing check listed only button and input while its implicit-role table listed four elements, and no binding renders a <textarea>, so the disagreement has never been observable. Fixing it is a behaviour change and belongs in its own commit.

visibility._note: `closesItself` is the load-bearing field: the platform writes this element's state behind the component's back, so a backend that only WRITES visibility and never reads it back will desync permanently and the element can never be shown again. `reflects` names the attribute to observe. `supplies` lists the four behaviours a backend WITHOUT this element owes by hand, so the omission is visible rather than assumed.

dialog._note: Same implicitRole/bearsRole disagreement as textarea, and unobservable for the same kind of reason: Dialog's contract declares `role: "dialog"` on its anatomy root, which satisfies the role-bearing check by the other branch.

a._note: Transcribed as unconditionally focusable. On the platform it is focusable only WITH an href. No binding renders an anchor, so the simplification has never been exercised.

states._doc: A contract's state name, and the channels the platform offers for carrying it. An entry says what is POSSIBLE; which channel WINS is a decision, and lives in resolve.mjs.

read-only._note: NO `native` key, deliberately. The platform has a `readonly` attribute on input and textarea, and adding it here would reroute TextField's read-only state from aria-readonly to the native attribute. TextField currently emits BOTH — aria-readonly from this table and readOnly from the natively-edited block — which is the duplication packages/react/src/emit/README.md section 2 warns against. Recorded, not fixed.

aria._doc: Keyed by ATTRIBUTE, because that is how WAI-ARIA defines these facts, and because two contract words may map to one attribute. An entry with no `roles` places no role restriction — which is this profile's position rather than the specification's, and is marked as such on each one.

aria-expanded._note: INCOMPLETE against WAI-ARIA 1.2, which also lists application, checkbox, listbox and switch. Transcribed as found. Completing it is a behaviour change — it would let a switch that also declares `open` acquire aria-expanded — so it needs its own commit and its own diff.

aria-disabled._note: No `roles`, so treated as unrestricted. OURS, not the specification's: aria-disabled is supported per role, not global. It has never mattered because `disabled` is also the one state allowed to reach ARIA on an element carrying no role at all.

aria-invalid._note: No `roles`, so treated as unrestricted. Ours, as above.

aria-readonly._note: No `roles`, so treated as unrestricted. Ours, as above. RadioGroup emits aria-readonly on role=radiogroup on the strength of it.

valueWords._doc: A contract's state VALUES are its own words; ARIA has its own. Global rather than nested under a state, because the mapping applies to any valued state. A word absent here passes through unchanged.

relations._doc: A contract's word for a relationship between parts, and the ARIA attribute that carries it.

range._doc: A numeric state's facets, and the ARIA attributes that announce them.

visibility._doc: How the platform hides something that has no element of its own to do it.
visibility._note: `outrankedByAuthorStyles` is why an emitted stylesheet must write `display: none !important`. `[hidden] { display: none }` comes from the UA stylesheet and any author `display` beats it — the cascade trap that shipped a permanently-visible Dialog.
